image.name: scummvm
image.description: [ScummVM](https://www.scummvm.org/) is a program which allows you to run certain classic graphical adventure and role-playing games, provided you already have their data files. The clever part about this: ScummVM just replaces the executables shipped with the games, allowing you to play them on systems for which they were never designed! ScummVM is a complete rewrite of these games' executables and is not an emulator.

changelog.desc: Update for Selkies v2, default to X11 for cursor.
Rebase to Debian Trixie, make Wayland default disable with PIXELFLUX_WAYLAND=false.
Rebase to Ubuntu Noble, add wayland init.

volumes.desc: Users home directory in the container, stores local files and settings

ports.desc: HTTP ScummVM desktop gui must be proxied.

security_opt.desc: For Docker Engine only, many modern gui apps need this to function on older hosts as syscalls are unknown to Docker.

image.title: Scummvm
image.setup_instructions:
The application can be accessed at:

* https://yourhost:3001/

**The cursor double renders during gameplay, you can use "gaming mode" in the sidebar to get around this.**

snippets.docker_compose:
---
services:
  scummvm:
    image: ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/scummvm:latest
    container_name: scummvm
    security_opt:
      - seccomp:unconfined #optional
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=Etc/UTC
    volumes:
      - /path/to/config:/config
    ports:
      - 3000:3000
      - 3001:3001
    restart: unless-stopped
snippets.docker_run:
docker run -d \
  --name=scummvm \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined `#optional` \
  -e PUID=1000 \
  -e PGID=1000 \
  -e TZ=Etc/UTC \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -p 3001:3001 \
  -v /path/to/config:/config \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/scummvm:latest
